headline: Highest risk is medium: Flowise can write/read shared files and egress broadly, while langchain4j is network-isolated and undocumented for pairwise interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read and write the server filesystem and uploaded files, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content as trusted input. langchain4j has no documented shared channel or file surface here, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and uncertain; per rubric, uncertainty escalates above low because a shared workspace is plausible in deployment.
conditions: IF Flowise ingests files or uploaded content produced by langchain4j without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents are deployed against the same shared workspace, cross-agent instruction smuggling becomes feasible.
mitigations: Disable shared filesystem access between the agents.
Add provenance tags and strip instructions from file inputs.
Require explicit allowlists for any file or upload consumed by Flowise.
Run langchain4j in a separate workspace with no write access.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, uploaded files, and tool credentials, and it has broad network egress. langchain4j shows no egress and no data classes touched, so the main leakage path is Flowise exporting sensitive context to external model providers or HTTP tools; the pairwise risk is medium because the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Flowise routes uploaded files or chatflow outputs to external model providers or HTTP tools, those contents can leave the environment.
IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets, Flowise can read them and transmit them via configured tools.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Restrict Flowise tool credentials to least privilege.
Disable or tightly scope HTTP/search tools in Flowise flows.
Use separate service accounts and storage buckets.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP scanning on Flowise outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can read and write the server filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared state via a server datastore. langchain4j is not documented here as writing anything, but the pair still has a plausible write-conflict path if both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or datastore; uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore, file or state conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, concurrent Flowise instances can overwrite each other's state.
mitigations: Separate writable directories per agent.
Turn on datastore or file locking in the orchestrator.
Avoid sharing git or database state between agents.
Schedule writes so only one agent mutates a resource at a time.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs and model responses, while langchain4j is a customer-support integration layer with no documented verification step here. If langchain4j consumes Flowise output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions; the interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF langchain4j uses Flowise output as a final answer without independent validation, hallucinations can propagate.
IF Flowise-generated facts are used to trigger customer-support actions, incorrect actions may follow.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking.
Require citations or source links for Flowise-generated claims.
Have langchain4j re-check critical facts against source systems.
Limit Flowise output to suggestions, not decisions.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise explicitly handles model provider keys and tool credentials and can process chatflow inputs/outputs, but langchain4j shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention mismatch is documented. The only concrete compliance concern is local handling of secrets by Flowise; the pairwise residency/compliance breach is not established, so low fits.
conditions: IF Flowise is configured to process regulated data through external model providers, compliance obligations may apply.
IF shared logs retain secrets from Flowise chatflows, retention policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Flowise flows.
Rotate and redact any exposed tool credentials.
Shorten log retention on Flowise outputs.
Confirm vendor DPAs before sending sensitive data externally.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing and retention controls.
